learning_objective: 🎯 Understand what authority is, how it differs from raw power, and why people choose to obey rules and leaders in a society!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: वैधता (सही या कानूनी होने का भाव)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Power is the ability to force someone to do something, even against their will (like a bully). Authority is 'legitimate power'—when people willingly obey because they believe the person has the right to give orders (like a teacher or a police officer).
Authority based on long-standing customs and traditions. People obey because 'it has always been this way.' Examples: A king, a tribal chief, or the eldest member of a family.
Authority based on the extraordinary personal qualities or heroism of a leader. People obey because they are deeply inspired by the person. Examples: Mahatma Gandhi, Nelson Mandela.

Authority based on written laws and rules. You obey the position, not the person. If a police officer is off-duty and out of uniform, they don't have the same authority. Example: A Prime Minister or a Judge.
In a democracy, no authority is absolute. Authority is limited by a Constitution to ensure leaders do not misuse their power and citizens' rights remain protected.

fun_activity.title: 👑 The Authority Map
fun_activity.instructions: Think about your normal day. Write down one person who exercises 'Traditional Authority' over you (e.g., a grandparent) and one person who exercises 'Legal-Rational Authority' over you (e.g., the school principal)!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define Authority as 'Power + Legitimacy'. Without legitimacy, authority is just raw force.
📌 Max Weber is the sociologist who classified authority into three types (Traditional, Charismatic, Legal-Rational). Memorize these three types!
📌 Modern democracies run primarily on Legal-Rational authority, meaning the law is supreme, not the individual.
quick_recap: ⭐ A dictator relies on fear and power; a democratic leader relies on legitimate authority given by voters.
⭐ Charismatic authority is often unstable because it relies entirely on one individual's lifespan and popularity.
⭐ Rules are easier to enforce when people believe the rule-maker has legitimate authority.
